purpose: Tie a future nonlinear likelihood representation to posterior probability error instead of a voltage materiality heuristic.
assumptions: Exact P and approximate Q use the same prior, parameterization, support and target map.
Both normalizers are positive and finite and likelihoods are positive on their common essential support.
The parameter-dependent log likelihood error delta=ell-ell_hat satisfies a<=delta<=b throughout that support, almost everywhere.

definitions.width: w=b-a is the oscillation of log likelihood error.

identities_and_bounds.event: For every event A with q=Q(A), L(q,w)<=P(A)<=U(q,w).
identities_and_bounds.log_odds: For0<q<1, |logit(P(A))-logit(Q(A))|<=w. At q=0 or1, common support forces equality.
identities_and_bounds.credible_region: If Q(C)>=1-alpha_hat, then P(C_complement)<=U(alpha_hat,w). Requiring alpha_hat<=L(alpha,w) suffices for P(C)>=1-alpha. No alpha or error budget is selected here.

proof.event: Let r_A=E_Q[exp(delta)|A], r_C=E_Q[exp(delta)|A_complement]. Both lie in[exp(a),exp(b)]. Then p=q*r_A/[q*r_A+(1-q)*r_C]. Extreme allowed ratios give L and U and attain the bounds.
proof.TV: Maximizing U(q,w)-q over q gives q=1/[1+exp(w/2)] and maximum[exp(w/2)-1]/[exp(w/2)+1]=tanh(w/4). The lower difference is symmetric.

composition.validity: For a valid exact factorization of disjoint observation blocks, sum_i a_i<=delta_total<=sum_i b_i, hence w_total<=sum_i(b_i-a_i). Conditional independence or correctly conditioned chain-rule factors are needed; disjoint IDs alone do not establish a likelihood factorization.
composition.replacement: Relinearizing or replacing an old evidence block replaces its earlier representation. Never append the same observations or combine them with their derived posterior as independent evidence.
composition.offsets: An additive error constant over the entire unknown state cancels in normalized posterior inference. Component-specific constants change mixture weights and do not cancel globally. Absolute evidence offsets must remain available if model evidence is needed.
composition.boundary_states: Approximate entering-state distributions, latent-history marginalization and changed conditioning laws must be included in the block's error account.
composition.lifetime: Repeated positive allowances can accumulate until the bound becomes uninformative; a future streaming design must own its cumulative error. No per-step allowance is chosen here.

limits: A local Hessian, finite grid, small prediction difference or narrow Gaussian factor does not provide the global error premise.
Deleting positive-likelihood support creates unbounded log error. A certificate restricted to a retained region additionally needs an omitted-mass bound for unconditional inference.
Changed priors or target maps need their own error accounting.
These bounds compare two specified model posteriors. They do not establish correctness of the physical/noise model or frequentist coverage.
The current learner and the new pure-likelihood control have not been shown to satisfy this certificate.
